Regulation of Student Financial Aid Programs
paragraphs: To provide access to higher education opportunities that enable students to develop the knowledge and skills necessary to achieve their professional goals, improve the performance of their organizations and provide leadership and service to their communities.

We are a mission-driven organization operating at the forefront of the rapidly evolving post-secondary education market. As one of the largest online education providers and a pioneer in our field, we benefit from the dynamic interplay between technological innovation, education, employment and economic trends. The demands of the modern workforce are continually shifting, and we are focused on transforming the way individuals achieve their educational and career aspirations while balancing the unique demands of being an adult learner. We are focused on delivering a personalized, career-relevant and affordable education to our students through our flexible learning model, skills-aligned curriculum and accessible tuition costs. We have created purpose-built platforms that leverage an AI-ready data infrastructure and technology stack to enhance the student experience, increase student success and improve the connectivity between students, educators and employers.

The University of Phoenix was founded in 1976 and has been continuously accredited since 1978 by The Higher Learning Commission (“HLC”), an institutional accrediting agency recognized by the U.S. Department of Education. In our nearly five decades of operation, as of August 31, 2025, we have served more than 1.1 million alumni (including those who have completed non-degree certificates) and conferred nearly 1.3 million degrees.

Our student body consists primarily of working adults seeking to advance their careers. Adult learners represent an attractive and growing sub-segment of the higher education market. However, they face unique challenges that are not addressed by traditional programs designed for 18- to 22-year-olds, including the time constraints and responsibilities of work, community and caring for dependents. As a result, these students can significantly benefit from an education solution tailored to their needs. We are dedicated to these adult learners, and we are constantly evolving the flexible, asynchronous learning models and the robust technology solutions designed to meet their unique needs. We believe we provide a differentiated value proposition to both students and employers. Both inside and outside of the classroom, our purpose is to help our students achieve their educational and career goals and to assist employers in upskilling their employees.

For the fiscal year ended August 31, 2025, the University’s Average Total Degreed Enrollment was 81,900, including 66,300 undergraduate and 15,600 graduate students. See Item 7, “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” for the definition of Average Total Degreed Enrollment. Students either enroll at the University independently or have the option to enroll through our employer relationships. Many of our students receive discounted tuition benefits under programs offered through our employer relationships, which are classified as B2B enrollment. These include students who enroll in the University through employer-provided programs, as well as students who enroll independently but are employees of employers with whom we have an employer relationship. Enrollment through our employer relationships represented approximately 32% of our Average Total Degreed Enrollment in fiscal year 2025.

The University currently offers 72 degree-granting and 33 non-degree certificate programs across a wide range of disciplines, including business and information technology (“IT”), health professions, social and behavioral sciences, education, nursing, doctoral studies and general studies. Our degree-granting programs represented approximately 97% of our net revenue for fiscal year 2025 and serve a diverse set of students who are seeking to improve their career opportunities:
Average Total Degreed Enrollment by degree type for fiscal year 2025: • Bachelor’s: 70%
Of the University’s enrollment during fiscal year 2025, subject to data availability for each metric:
• 75% are currently employed; • 95% of new students are over the age of 22, with an average age of 38;
• 53% are first-generation college students;
• 62% of students who completed an optional survey identify as members of a minority group; and

Our non-degree offerings for students and employers represent the remaining portion of net revenue and are a growing priority for the University. These non-degree offerings include shorter credit-bearing certificates and non-credit professional development courses that provide students with critical skills for career advancement and benefit employers by upskilling their employees.

We are also developing new talent solutions programs for employers, including: (i) a talent-sourcing platform that connects employers with students whose skills profiles align with job postings and (ii) an AI-powered tool that scans an employer’s inventory of sought-after skills and designs development pathways to internal job opportunities.

headings: Risks Related to the Highly Regulated Industry in Which We Operate
Shifts in higher education policy at the federal and state levels could have a material adverse effect on our business or render our current business impractical or unsustainable.
The University may lose eligibility to participate in Title IV programs if the percentage of our revenue derived from federal funding sources is too high.
paragraphs: You should carefully consider the risks and uncertainties described below, as well as the other information contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including our consolidated financial statements and the related notes thereto and “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations.” Additional risks not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial may also affect us. If any of these risks occur, our business, financial condition or results of operations could be materially and adversely affected. Further, past financial performance may not be a reliable indicator of future performance and historical trends should not be used to anticipate results or trends in future periods.
This summary briefly lists the principal risks and uncertainties facing our business, which are only a select portion of those risks:

• we operate in a highly regulated industry with extensive regulatory requirements, and the failure to comply with applicable regulations or regulatory requirements, standards or policies could subject us to significant monetary liabilities, fines and penalties, including loss of or limitations upon access to U.S. federal student loans, grants and military program benefits for our students, and otherwise have a material adverse impact on our business;

• the impact that recent amendments to the Higher Education Act by Congress may have on our business, including the recent amendments that will limit or reduce the amount of federal student aid funding and that condition the future eligibility of educational programs for federal student aid funding upon compliance with new metrics focused upon the earnings of our former students;
• risks associated with the impact that further legislative, political and regulatory changes could have on our business;

• the impact that the loss of institutional accreditation, loss of, or failure to receive, certifications for participation in Title IV programs or limitations imposed by the Department of Education or state regulatory authorities could have on our business;

paragraphs: 為提供學生進修高等教育的機會，使其得以發展知識與技能，以達成其專業目標、提升其組織的表現，並為其社區提供領導與服務，本公司致力於此目標。

本公司為一個以使命為導向的組織，處於快速演變的後續教育市場的最前線。作為最大的線上教育服務提供者之一，並在該領域中開創先河，我們受益於科技創新、教育、就業與經濟趨勢之間的動態互動。現代勞動市場的需求持續變化，我們專注於改變個人實現教育與職業目標的方式，同時平衡成人學習者獨特的壓力。我們專注於透過靈活的學習模式、與技能對應的課程以及可負擔的學費，為學生提供個性化、與職業相關且經濟實惠的教育。我們已建立專為此目的設計的平台，這些平台利用AI就緒的數據基礎設施與科技架構，以提升學生的學習體驗、提高學生的成功率，並改善學生、教育者與僱主之間的連接。
鳳凰大學於1976年成立，自1978年起持續獲得美國教育部認可的機構認證機構「高等教育委員會」（Higher Learning Commission，簡稱HLC）認證。在近五十年的運作中，截至2025年8月31日，我們已服務超過1.1百萬校友（包括完成非學位證書的學生），並頒發近1.3百萬學位。

我們的學生主要為尋求進修以提升職業的在職成人。成人學習者代表高等教育市場中一個具吸引力且成長中的子市場。然而，他們面臨傳統為18至22歲學生設計的課程所無法解決的獨特挑戰，包括工作、社區及照顧取決者所帶來的時間限制與責任。因此，這些學生可從為其需求量身打造的教育解決方案中獲益良多。我們致力於這些成人學習者，並持續改進靈活、非同步的學習模式與強大科技解決方案，以符合其獨特需求。我們相信，我們為學生與僱主提供了獨特的價值主張。無論課堂內外，我們的目標都是協助學生達成其教育與職業目標，並協助僱主提升員工技能。

會計年度終了日為2025年8月31日，本校的平均總註冊學生數為81,900人，其中包括66,300名大學部學生及15,600名研究所學生。有關平均總註冊學生數的定義，請參閱第7項「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析」。學生可自行向本校註冊，或透過我們的僱主關係進行註冊。許多學生透過我們的僱主關係所提供的計畫，獲得學費折扣福利，這些被歸類為B2B註冊。這些包括透過僱主提供計畫註冊本校的學生，以及雖為自行註冊但為與我們有僱主關係之僱主員工的學生。透過我們的僱主關係進行註冊，約佔我們2025會計年度平均總註冊學生數的32%。
本校目前提供72個頒發學位的課程及33個非學位證書課程，涵蓋廣泛的學科領域，包括商業與資訊科技（「IT」）、醫療專業、社會與行為科學、教育、護理、博士學位研究及一般研究。我們的學位課程約佔我們2025會計年度淨營收的97%，服務多樣化的學生，這些學生希望提升自己的職業機會：
2025會計年度平均總註冊學生數按學位類型分類： • 學士：70%
於財務年度 2025 年，就大學 enrolment 數量而言，各指標之資料尚待取得：
本公司針對學生與僱主所提供之非學位課程，代表淨營收之剩餘部分，並為大學之成長重點。這些非學位課程包含較短之學分證書及非學分之專業發展課程，可提供學生關鍵之職業進修技能，並使僱主能透過提升員工技能而受益。

headings: 與我們經營的嚴格管制產業相關的風險
聯邦及州級高等教育政策的變動可能對我們的業務造成重大不利影響，或使我們目前的業務變得不實際或不可持續。
若本公司來自聯邦資金來源的收入佔比過高，大學可能喪失參與 Title IV 計畫的資格。
